crops.name: Onion
crops.overview: Onion is a cool-season bulb vegetable grown for fresh sale and storage. Maharashtra is one of India's largest onion-producing states, with crops in kharif, late kharif and rabi seasons.
crops.sowing: Kharif: May–July (nursery), transplant June–August. Late kharif: August–October. Rabi: October–December (nursery), transplant November–January.
crops.soil: Well-drained loamy or sandy loam soil, pH about 6.0–7.5. Avoid waterlogged or heavy clay soil.
crops.climate: Needs cool weather while the plant grows leaves and a warmer, drier period for bulb maturity.
crops.irrigation: Light, frequent irrigation, especially during bulb formation. Stop irrigation some days before harvest so bulbs cure well.
crops.nutrients: Responds to balanced nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium and sulphur. Confirm quantities against your soil test and local agriculture department advice.
crops.harvest: Ready when about half to three-quarters of the tops fall over and necks soften, usually 100–150 days after transplanting depending on season and variety.
crops.storage: Cure bulbs in shade for a few days, keep them dry, and store in well-ventilated structures. Remove damaged or sprouting bulbs.

crops.name: Soybean
crops.overview: Soybean is a major kharif oilseed and protein crop in Maharashtra, mostly grown rain-fed.
crops.sowing: Kharif: mid June to mid July, once the monsoon has given good, steady rain.
crops.soil: Well-drained medium to deep black or loamy soil, pH about 6.0–7.5. Poorly drained fields suffer in heavy rain.
crops.climate: Warm and moist growing season; needs adequate rain or irrigation at flowering and pod filling.
crops.irrigation: Usually rain-fed. If there is a long dry spell, a protective irrigation at flowering or pod filling helps.
crops.nutrients: Seed treatment with a suitable Rhizobium culture is commonly advised. Fertilizer should follow a soil test and local recommendations.
crops.harvest: Harvest when leaves turn yellow and drop and pods are dry, about 90–110 days depending on variety.
crops.storage: Dry grain to a safe moisture level before storing. Store in clean, dry, pest-free bags or bins.

crops.name: Wheat
crops.overview: Wheat is the main rabi cereal, grown on residual soil moisture or with irrigation.
crops.sowing: Rabi: November to mid December for timely sowing; late sowing gives lower yield.
crops.soil: Well-drained loam to clay loam, pH about 6.0–7.5.
crops.climate: Cool weather during growth and a warm, dry period at grain filling. High temperature at grain filling can reduce yield.
crops.irrigation: Critical stages are crown root initiation, tillering, jointing, flowering and grain filling. Number of irrigations depends on soil and variety.
crops.nutrients: Needs nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium; split nitrogen application is common. Follow soil test and local recommendations.
crops.harvest: Harvest when grain is hard and straw turns golden-yellow, about 110–130 days after sowing.
crops.storage: Store only well-dried grain in clean, moisture-proof containers. Check regularly for weevils.

crops.name: Rice
crops.overview: Rice is a kharif cereal grown under transplanted, direct-seeded or rain-fed conditions.
crops.sowing: Kharif: nursery in June, transplanting in July after good rain.
crops.soil: Clay or clay loam that holds water; pH about 5.5–7.0.
crops.climate: Warm and humid. Needs plentiful water, especially from tillering to flowering.
crops.irrigation: Keep the field moist to shallowly flooded during growth; drain before harvest. Water-saving methods such as alternate wetting and drying can reduce use.
crops.nutrients: Nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium in split doses are common. Zinc is often deficient. Use soil test results.
crops.harvest: Harvest when about 80–85% of grains in the panicle are straw-coloured, roughly 110–150 days depending on variety.
crops.storage: Dry paddy to a safe moisture level before storage. Keep it off the floor and away from damp walls.

crops.name: Tomato
crops.overview: Tomato is a warm-season fruit vegetable grown for fresh market and processing.
crops.sowing: Kharif: June–July. Rabi: September–November. Summer: January–February.
crops.soil: Well-drained loam or sandy loam rich in organic matter, pH about 6.0–7.0.
crops.climate: Grows best at moderate temperatures; very hot or very cold weather reduces fruit set.
crops.irrigation: Regular, even moisture. Irregular watering can cause fruit cracking and blossom-end problems.
crops.nutrients: Needs balanced nutrients and calcium; staking and organic matter help. Follow soil test advice.
crops.harvest: First picking about 60–90 days after transplanting; pick at the maturity stage suited to the distance to market.
crops.storage: Handle gently. Keep in a cool, ventilated place; fully ripe tomatoes keep only a few days.

crops.name: Cotton
crops.overview: Cotton is a long-duration kharif fibre crop, widely grown in Maharashtra, largely rain-fed.
crops.sowing: Kharif: June–July with the onset of the monsoon; irrigated crops may be sown earlier.
crops.soil: Deep, well-drained black cotton soil (regur) or medium loam, pH about 6.0–8.0.
crops.climate: Warm climate with enough moisture at flowering and boll formation; dry weather at picking.
crops.irrigation: Mostly rain-fed; irrigation at flowering and boll development protects yield during dry spells.
crops.nutrients: Needs nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium; avoid over-use of nitrogen which promotes pests. Follow soil test advice.
crops.harvest: Pick open bolls in several rounds, usually starting 150–180 days after sowing.
crops.storage: Keep picked cotton dry and clean, free of leaf and soil, and store off the ground.

crops.name: Sugarcane
crops.overview: Sugarcane is a long-duration cash crop. Most Maharashtra crop is supplied to sugar factories.
crops.sowing: Adsali: July–August (about 16–18 months). Pre-seasonal: October–November. Suru: January–February.
crops.soil: Deep, well-drained loam or clay loam, pH about 6.5–7.5.
crops.climate: Warm, sunny climate with plenty of water; cool dry weather near harvest improves sugar content.
crops.irrigation: Needs regular irrigation. Drip irrigation can save water and improve efficiency.
crops.nutrients: High nutrient demand. Organic matter and soil-test-based fertilizer are advised.
crops.harvest: Harvest when the crop is mature, as advised by the sugar factory, usually 10–18 months after planting depending on the planting season.
crops.storage: Deliver cane to the factory quickly after cutting; sugar content falls with delay.

crops.name: Chilli
crops.overview: Chilli is a spice and vegetable crop grown for green and dry sale.
crops.sowing: Kharif: nursery May–June, transplant June–July. Rabi: nursery September–October.
crops.soil: Well-drained loam or black soil rich in organic matter, pH about 6.0–7.5.
crops.climate: Warm, humid climate; very high temperature or heavy rain at flowering can cause flower drop.
crops.irrigation: Light, frequent irrigation. Avoid water stress at flowering and fruit set, and avoid waterlogging.
crops.nutrients: Needs balanced nutrients with attention to potassium and calcium. Follow soil test advice.
crops.harvest: Green chilli can be picked from about 60–75 days after transplanting; for dry chilli, pick fully red, ripe fruit.
crops.storage: Dry red chilli thoroughly in clean, shaded or protected conditions and store in dry, ventilated bags.

crops.name: Potato
crops.overview: Potato is a cool-season tuber crop, grown in Maharashtra mainly in rabi and in some cooler hill areas.
crops.soil: Loose, well-drained sandy loam or loam, pH about 5.5–6.5.
crops.climate: Cool weather (moderate night temperature) for tuber formation; hot conditions reduce tuber growth.
crops.irrigation: Light, regular irrigation, especially during tuber initiation and bulking. Avoid waterlogging.
crops.nutrients: Needs nitrogen, phosphorus and considerable potassium. Follow soil test advice.
crops.harvest: Harvest when vines dry and skins are firm, about 75–110 days depending on variety.
crops.storage: Cure in shade, sort out damaged tubers, and store cool, dark and ventilated; cold storage is used for long storage.

crops.name: Maize
crops.overview: Maize is grown as grain, fodder and sweet corn in kharif and rabi.
crops.sowing: Kharif: June–July with the monsoon. Rabi: October–November.
crops.soil: Well-drained fertile loam, pH about 6.0–7.5. Sensitive to waterlogging.
crops.climate: Warm season crop; needs adequate moisture at tasselling and silking.
crops.irrigation: Critical stages are knee-high, tasselling, silking and grain filling. Avoid stress at these stages.
crops.nutrients: Responds strongly to nitrogen in split doses, with phosphorus and potassium as per soil test.
crops.harvest: Harvest when husks dry and grains are hard, about 90–120 days for grain maize.
crops.storage: Dry grain thoroughly to a safe moisture level before storage to prevent mould and toxins.
